37	`/opt/homebrew/var/lib/jenkins`, despite what some older docs say). Get the
38	initial admin password with:
39	
40	```
41	cat ~/.jenkins/secrets/initialAdminPassword
42	```
43	
44	**Linux:** follow the [official Jenkins Linux install
45	instructions](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/installing/linux/) for your
46	distro (e.g. the `apt`/`yum` package repo), then start it via `systemctl
47	start jenkins` (most distros enable/start it automatically on install).
48	`JENKINS_HOME` is `/var/lib/jenkins` by default. Get the initial admin
49	password with:
50	
51	```
52	sudo cat /var/lib/jenkins/secrets/initialAdminPassword
53	```
54	
55	**Both:** Jenkins listens on `http://localhost:8080`. Open it, paste the
56	password, and install the "suggested plugins" set when prompted.
57	
58	## 2. Install additional plugins
59	
60	Manage Jenkins → Plugins → Available plugins, install:
61	
62	- **GitHub Branch Source** — lets Jenkins discover branches/PRs on a GitHub
63	  repo and is the GitHub equivalent of the Bitbucket Branch Source plugin
64	  SUNDIALS uses.
65	- **Collapsing Console Sections** (optional) — collapses long build log
66	  sections for readability, same as SUNDIALS' setup.
67	
68	## 3. Add a GitHub credential
69	
70	Jenkins needs read access to `gkeyllorg/gkeyll` to poll for branches and PRs:
71	
72	1. Create a GitHub Personal Access Token with `repo` scope (Settings →
73	   Developer settings → Personal access tokens on GitHub).
74	2. In Jenkins: Manage Jenkins → Credentials → System → Global credentials →
75	   Add Credentials → kind "GitHub personal access token" (or "Username with
76	   password", username = your GitHub username, password = the token).
77	
78	## 3a. Scope your controller to its own nodes
79	
80	`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile` has a single `nodes` map listing every known build
81	node across every independent controller that builds this repo (yours and
82	anyone else's). This keeps that map a shared, PR-reviewable source of truth
83	— but it also means your controller must be told which of those labels it
84	actually owns agents for, or it will try to start a `node(label)` block for
85	someone else's node and hang forever waiting for an executor that will never
86	exist under your controller.
87	
88	Manage Jenkins → System → Global properties → check "Environment variables"
89	→ Add:
90	
91	- Name: `CI_OWNED_NODE_LABELS`
92	- Value: a comma-separated list of the node label(s) *this controller* owns,
93	  e.g. `manauref_lt1`, or `alice_laptop,alice_workstation` if you register
94	  more than one node under your own controller.
95	
96	This is a controller-wide setting — set it once, regardless of how many
97	nodes your controller owns. If it's unset (or blank), the pipeline fails
98	fast with an error telling you to set it, rather than hanging; that's
99	expected the first time you set up a new controller.
100	
101	## 4. Add a build node
102	
103	Every machine that runs builds — including the controller's own machine — is
104	a Jenkins "node" with a label matching one used in `ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`'s
105	`nodes` map. This procedure is the same whether you're setting up
106	`manauref_lt1` (the first node) or adding another machine later.
107	
108	### 4.1. Register the node and label it
109	
110	- **This machine** (the controller itself, e.g. `manauref_lt1`): Manage
111	  Jenkins → Nodes → "Built-In Node" → Configure → Labels: add the label.
112	- **A separate machine** (e.g. a workstation): Manage Jenkins → Nodes → New
113	  Node → "Permanent Agent" → Launch method "Launch agents via SSH",
114	  host/credentials for that machine, and give it a label. Nothing to install
115	  there yourself — Jenkins pushes its agent jar over SSH. Make sure Java, a
116	  C/C++/Fortran toolchain, and `cmake` are present; `mkdeps` builds everything
117	  else from scratch per build.
118	
119	This label is what the Jenkinsfile's `node('<label>')` matches.
120	
121	### 4.2. Fix the node's `PATH`
122	
123	On **macOS**, Jenkins runs as a `launchd` service (via `brew services`),
124	which does **not** source your shell profile (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`) —
125	so it starts with launchd's bare-bones default `PATH`
126	(`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`) and can't find Homebrew tools like `cmake`,
127	even though `which cmake` works fine in your terminal.
128	
129	On **Linux**, the built-in node's agent process is started by `systemd`
130	(via the `jenkins` service), which likewise does not source your shell
131	profile — it uses whatever minimal `PATH` is baked into the unit's
132	environment, which typically misses anything installed under `/opt`, a
133	package manager outside the base distro repos, or `$HOME`. An SSH-launched
134	agent on another machine (either OS) has its own, similar set of environment
135	quirks to sort out, since `sshd` non-interactive sessions don't source
136	`~/.bashrc`/`~/.zshrc` either.
137	
138	Fix this per-node in Jenkins itself (not by editing the launchd plist,
139	systemd unit, or a shell profile) so it works the same way regardless of how
140	each node's agent process is started, and each node keeps its own value —
141	this generalizes cleanly as you add more, across OSes.
142	
143	Manage Jenkins → Nodes → `<label>` → Configure → Node Properties → check
144	"Environment variables" → Add:
145	
146	- Name: `PATH`
147	- Value: wherever this node's build tools (`cmake`, compilers, MPI, a
148	  `python` with `numpy`, etc.) actually live, e.g.:
149	  - macOS (`manauref_lt1`):
150	    `/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`
151	  - Linux: typically
152	    `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, plus anywhere your
153	    toolchain/MPI/Python were installed outside the base distro repos (e.g.
154	    `/opt/<something>/bin`, a Conda/venv `bin`, or `/usr/local/cuda/bin`).
155	
156	Don't assume this matches another node's value — especially across OSes.
157	
158	### 4.3. Personal machine or team machine?
159	
160	- **Personal computer** (like `manauref_lt1`): the multibranch job builds —
161	  i.e. executes — the code of any PR opened against the repo, on whichever
162	  node picks it up. On a personal machine you probably don't want to run
163	  other contributors' PR code, so restrict this node to PRs you authored: in
164	  `ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`, add `allowedPrAuthors: ['<your-github-username>']`
165	  to this node's entry in the `nodes` map. PR builds from any other author
166	  are skipped on this node (logged in the console, not failed); builds of
167	  `main` itself are unaffected, since there's no PR author to check there.
168	  Note this is a Jenkinsfile-level control, not a GitHub-side protection — it
169	  only takes effect once Jenkins has already scanned and started that node's
170	  branch of the pipeline.
171	- **Shared/team machine**: omit `allowedPrAuthors` from its entry — it will
172	  build PRs from anyone.
173	
174	### 4.4. Register the node in the Jenkinsfile
175	
176	Add (or confirm) an entry in the `nodes` map in `ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`,
177	using whichever `mkdeps`/`configure` scripts under `machines/` match that
178	node's OS:
179	
180	```groovy
181	def nodes = [
182	    'manauref_lt1': [mkdeps: 'mkdeps.macos.sh', configure: 'configure.macos.sh', allowedPrAuthors: ['manauref']],
183	    'workstation-node': [mkdeps: 'mkdeps.linux.sh', configure: 'configure.linux.cpu.sh'],
184	]
185	```
186	
187	Commit and push (a normal PR against `main`, same as any other change).
188	Adding a node's entry to this shared map doesn't by itself make any
189	controller build on it — only a controller whose `CI_OWNED_NODE_LABELS`
190	(step 3a) includes this label will. The next PR build will then run on every
191	node your controller owns, in parallel (subject to each node's
192	`allowedPrAuthors`, if set).
193	
194	## 5. Nothing to pre-build
195	
196	Unlike an earlier version of this setup, the pipeline does **not** assume a
197	pre-built `gkylsoft/` on any node. Each build passes
198	`PREFIX=$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft` to that node's `mkdeps`/`configure` scripts, so
199	dependencies are built from scratch inside that build's own Jenkins
200	workspace — isolated from any manual checkout you have elsewhere, and safe
201	for concurrent builds of different branches/PRs on the same node (each gets
202	its own workspace, so its own `gkylsoft/`).
203	
204	The tradeoff is build time: expect each build to spend several extra minutes
205	building SuperLU/LuaJIT from source before it even gets to compiling Gkeyll,
206	same as `.github/workflows/mac_build.yml` does on GitHub's runners.
207	
208	You still need a working toolchain, `cmake`, and a `python` on `PATH` with
209	`numpy` installed (used to process the ADAS atomic data some gyrokinetic
210	unit tests, e.g. `ctest_dg_iz`/`ctest_dg_recomb`, need at runtime) on each
211	node for its `mkdeps` script to succeed — if you've built Gkeyll manually on
212	that machine before, you already have most of these:
213	
214	- **macOS**: Xcode command line tools (`xcode-select --install`) for the
215	  C/C++/Fortran toolchain, plus `cmake`/`python` (e.g. via Homebrew).
216	- **Linux**: a C/C++/Fortran toolchain (e.g. `build-essential` + `gfortran`
217	  on Debian/Ubuntu, or the equivalent group on your distro), plus `cmake` and
218	  a `python` with `numpy` from your package manager (or a Conda/venv install,
219	  as long as it's on the `PATH` set in step 4.2).
220	
221	## 6. Create the multibranch pipeline job
222	
223	New Item → name it (e.g. `gkeyll`) → **Multibranch Pipeline**.
224	
225	- **Branch Sources** → Add source → GitHub:
226	  - Credentials: the one added in step 3.
227	  - Repository HTTPS URL: `https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkeyll`
228	  - Behaviors: "Discover branches" (at least `main`) and "Discover pull
229	    requests from origin". Add "Discover pull requests from forks" only if
230	    external contributors submit PRs from forks.
231	- **Build Configuration** → Mode: "by Jenkinsfile", Script Path:
232	  `ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`.
233	- **Scan Multibranch Pipeline Triggers** → check "Periodically if not
234	  otherwise run" → interval **2 minutes**.
235	
236	If your controller is behind NAT (as `manauref_lt1`'s is), GitHub can't push
237	a webhook to it. The periodic scan above is how Jenkins learns about
238	new/updated PRs instead — every 2 minutes it asks GitHub for changes and
239	kicks off a build if there are any. This means there's up to a ~2 minute
240	delay before a build starts, which is an acceptable tradeoff for not having
241	to run a public tunnel (e.g. ngrok) just to receive webhooks. If your
242	controller has a reachable public address, you can set up a GitHub webhook
243	instead for near-instant triggering — not covered here since none of our
244	controllers currently need it.
245	
246	Save. Jenkins will scan the repo, find `main` and any open PRs with a
247	Jenkinsfile, and start building them.
248	
249	## What the pipeline does
250	
251	First, the pipeline filters the shared `nodes` map down to just the label(s)
252	in this controller's own `CI_OWNED_NODE_LABELS` (step 3a) — failing fast if
253	that's not set. Then, per node this controller owns, in parallel (skipping a
254	node entirely if the PR's author isn't in that node's `allowedPrAuthors`,
255	when set):
256	
257	1. `printenv` — for debugging the build environment.
258	2. `make clean` and `rm -rf $WORKSPACE/gkylsoft` — the workspace persists
259	   across builds for a given branch/PR, so without this, a stale or (e.g.
260	   from a prior interrupted or racing build) corrupted file can look
261	   up-to-date and never get rebuilt/reinstalled, silently breaking the link
262	   or mixing old and new dependency files. Wiping both every run makes each
263	   build genuinely from scratch.
264	3. That node's `mkdeps` script (e.g. `machines/mkdeps.macos.sh`) — builds
265	   `gkylsoft/` from scratch into `$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft`.
266	4. That node's `configure` script (e.g. `machines/configure.macos.sh`) —
267	   generates `config.mak` pointing at that freshly-built `gkylsoft/`.
268	5. `make -j3 check` — builds **and runs** all unit tests (`core`, `moments`,
269	   `vlasov`, `gyrokinetic`, `pkpm`); a failing unit test fails the build.
270	6. `make -j3 regression` — builds (does not execute) all regression tests,
271	   matching today's `.github/workflows/mac_build.yml` scope. There is no
272	   automated regression-test runner yet; running a curated subset of
273	   regression tests is a follow-up.
274	7. Archives `build/**/*.log` so logs are downloadable from the Jenkins build
275	   page even on failure.
276
